messages:
alex: seeing tail-latency spikes on gpu-inference-prod - QPS steady but 95p/99p jump, HPA ramped pods to 18 and then 28 in 3m
maya: same, Grafana shows concurrent inflight up too. CA didn't provision nodes; lots of pods stuck Pending with GPU predicate failures
li: any k8s events? can you paste `kubectl describe` for one Pending pod?
alex: pasted below:
```
Name: inference-worker-5f9d7
Status: Pending
Events:
  Type     Reason            Age    From               Message
  ----     ------            ----   ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling  2m     default-scheduler  0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match node selector, 2 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate, 5 node(s) didn't have available GPUs, 3 Insufficient cpu.
```
li: looks like a couple things: nodeSelector mismatch and insufficient GPUs - probably we hit regional GPU quota on the cloud project so CA didn't create more GPU nodes. Also taint/toleration mismatch on some nodepools after the last deploy
ops-oncall: cloud quotas show GPUs at 100% in us-west1-b, but other zones have spare capacity. CA is zone-aware but our nodepool config pins pools to specific zones via helm chart right now.
maya: that explains why pod replicas increased (HPA responded to higher latency QPS metric) but CA couldn't add matching GPU nodes in that zone -> pod Pending -> backlog -> increased latency -> feedback loop
sre-bot: alert: HPA("inference-hpa") scaled from 12 -> 28 in 4m; pending pods 16; nodepool us-west1-b gpu-ptx-rt at quota.
alex: we should avoid HPA-triggered thundering in zones with tight quota. Options: 1) smooth HPA metric (increase window and stabilization), 2) change HPA to cross-zone aware metric (external metric that uses global inflight), 3) make CA able to fall back to non-GPU nodes with model-quantized variant, 4) pre-warm nodes in other zones. thoughts?
li: short-term: increase HPA scaleDown/stabilization window and add a maxReplica cap for that HPA for the next 1h. Also tweak external metric adapter to emit per-zone available-capacity so HPA can backoff.
maya: medium-term: implement a CA policy: when GPU quota in primary zone is exhausted, route new pods to a compatible nodepool in other zones (with autoscaler taint-matching), or trigger quick model fallback to a lower-vram variant on existing nodes. Need infra changes to nodepool manifest and a runtime model selector.
ops-oncall: can we also gate HPA by an external metric called `gpu_node_available_count`? if zero in zone, HPA should stop firing.
li: yes, Prometheus adapter can expose `external/gpu_available_{zone}` using kube-state-metrics + cloud API. I can wire that and add as a condition to the HPA using the external metrics support.
alex: adding the prometheus query I'm using to detect the problem:
```
(sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="inference",le!="+Inf"}[2m])) by (app)) /
(sum(inflight_requests_total{job="inference"}) by (app))
```
This ratio jumps when pending queue builds up.
maya: also noticed KV cache misses in logs to redis when pods are Pending -> new pods cold-start and requests fall back to upstream -> extra network egress to redis cluster in another region -> egress quota spikes.
ops-oncall: cloud egress to redis-secondary in us-central increased by 3x during the incident. We have egress caps per project. If egress hits cap, flows degrade and latency spikes.
alex: action list I'm going to run now: 1) patch HPA to set stabilizationWindowSeconds=120 and add maxReplicas=22, 2) create temporary PAUSE label on the deployment to stop rapid rollouts, 3) open a ticket to request GPU quota bump in us-west1-b if we want long-term.
maya: +1. Also put a Circuit Breaker: if pending_pods > 10 and gpu_available_zone == 0 then route new requests to async queue (SQS) and return 202 so clients degrade gracefully. We already have that pattern for batch fallbacks.
li: implementing prometheus-adapter metric now, ETA 30m. I'll also update the HPA manifest to include the external metric as a required condition.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: patch hpa/inference-hpa -> stabilizationWindowSeconds=120, maxReplicas=22 (rolling patch)

alex: applied patch, monitoring.
(some minutes later)
li: prometheus-adapter exposing `external/gpu_available_us-west1-b` = 0 now for 5m. HPA respects it and stopped scaling further. Pending pod count stabilized.
maya: started routing ~30% of incoming traffic to async queue via feature flag; 95p latency dropping.
ops-oncall: cloud egress reduced and redis errors decreased.
sre-bot: incident resolved? Recommend follow-ups: 1) modify nodepool provisioning to allow cross-zone fallback, 2) add egress budget alerting, 3) automate HPA guard with external metric, 4) consider always-on small warm-pool in secondary zone for bursts.
alex: agreed, I'll create follow-up tasks. Thanks all :thumbsup:
ops-oncall: logged follow-ups in TICKET-3482 (GPU quota / cross-zone fallback), TICKET-3483 (egress budget), TICKET-3484 (HPA external metric rollout)
li: leaving notes in the infra repo about taint compat and nodeSelector mismatch that contributed to the problem.
maya: nice quick mitigation. we'll review the long-term model fallback and costs tradeoff later.
